headline: The failure mode the task warned about is absent. The guide does not upgrade one pass into a guarantee, does not say the six items are now offline-provable, and does not claim the bridge is stable: it pins two timestamps, states three explicit limits, and explicitly refuses to upgrade 'one pass' to 'stably verified'. Its grading table still says pages=2 is offline-unprovable and 8/13 are reconstruction-only. I re-verified all nine protected token counts against the pre-change blob: identical. The one substantive new finding is external to the guide: at review time /health still reports edaConnected:true while /execute returns 500 'EDA window ... disconnected', so the record's expiry clause was not hypothetical - it fired within three minutes of the recorded runs.

observationBeyondTheReviewedArtifact.what: at review time the relay still reports edaConnected:true, edaWindowCount:1, activeWindowId 25883914a72e5cbb, while POST /execute returns HTTP 500 with body {"success":false,"error":"EDA window \"25883914a72e5cbb\" disconnected"} and pendingRequests:1
whyItMatters: it shows the expiry clause was not theoretical: the window's socket died within about three minutes of the recorded runs, so the record stopped being valid almost immediately

the expiry path is subtler than the guide's wording: the guide says '掉线' (window drops), and /health did NOT show a drop - it kept advertising the window. Only /execute knew. Anyone routing on /health alone would wrongly conclude the bridge was usable.
it exercises t53's branch (c) from the r8t5 taxonomy for the first time in the wild: window count >= 1, execute fails, reason BRIDGE_CALL_FAILED

it exposes a classification gap worth a follow-up: the message says 'disconnected', but t53's regex (/NO_EDA|not connected|edaConnected/) does not match 'disconnected', so a window-lost case is filed as a generic call failure. http-api.mjs's own matcher (L118: /no eda window connected|not connected|no longer connected/) misses it too. This is NOT a defect of the reviewed guide; it belongs to the error-classification owner.
observationBeyondTheReviewedArtifact.notClaimed: I am not treating this as evidence that the two exit-0 runs were false. They were real; what died afterwards is the registration, which is exactly what boundary 2 covers.

overall.why: All eight items pass. The specific risk - one pass inflated into a long-term guarantee - did not materialise: the file pins two timestamps, states three limits, and literally writes that one pass must not be upgraded to 'stably verified'. The grading table rows for pages 2 and 8/13 still say offline-unprovable and reconstruction-only, and a machine comparison of the pre-change and post-change blobs shows all nine protected token counts identical, with a single one-hunk diff at line 268 that cannot have touched the table at 255-263 or §D2/D3 above it. The git claims hold: HEAD = origin = cdfee6d, 0 0, clean.
overall.theOneThingIWouldStillImprove: the guide records a table, not a transcript. Committing the raw stdout of the two exit-0 runs (or pointing at an artifact that holds it) would let a third party check the timestamps without having to re-run a bridge that has since become unusable. That is an evidence-hygiene suggestion, not a correctness defect.

evidence.summary: The r2t1 guide change (the live-read record) is honest and bounded. Six elements present with both time zones, exit 0 and 5/5, 21/8/13/55/55/2, the componentType split with +3V3=part, the MAIN+P1 page table, the active page and the window id. Three limits present and phrased as limits; every overclaim phrase I grepped appears only inside a negation. The grading table's pages-2 and 8/13 rows are unchanged, proven by the single-hunk diff and by machine comparison of nine protected token counts between blobs 24774e0 and d382726 (all identical). Git state is 0 0 with HEAD = origin = cdfee6d, clean. A second t53 timestamp exists 36.213 s after the first with identical values, so the pair is internally consistent; no bare liveness claim is made.
